_comment: Agent orchestration rules for AI-powered content pipelines. How to use multiple AI models efficiently without burning tokens or producing garbage.

planning.use: Topic selection, content strategy, query analysis, growth review synthesis
planning.why: These decisions shape everything downstream. A bad topic choice wastes all downstream tokens. Use the best model for decisions that compound.

execution.use: Content writing, title generation, FAQ expansion, internal link insertion, data refreshes
execution.why: Writing quality from Sonnet is near-Opus at a fraction of the cost. Haiku handles mechanical tasks (reformatting, link checking, data extraction) at the lowest cost tier.

validation.use: Quality gate evaluation, template phrase detection, fact-checking against source URLs
validation.why: Validation needs good judgment but not maximum capability. Sonnet catches the same issues Opus would at lower cost.

orchestrationRules.noNestedSpawning: Never let an agent spawn sub-agents. The orchestrator controls all agent lifecycle.
orchestrationRules.failFast: If any quality gate fails, discard the entire piece. Don't spend tokens trying to fix content that failed basic checks — regenerate from scratch.

pipelineStages.name: Topic Selection
pipelineStages.input: GSC query gap data + existing content inventory + keyword anticipation calendar
pipelineStages.output: Ranked topic list with target queries and content format
pipelineStages.guard: Cannibalization check against existing content BEFORE writing

pipelineStages.name: Research
pipelineStages.input: Topic + target query + existing page (if refresh)
pipelineStages.output: Key data points, sources, current figures
pipelineStages.guard: Source URLs must be verified (HTTP 200, content matches claim)

pipelineStages.name: Writing
pipelineStages.input: Research output + voice/style rules + anti-AI rules
pipelineStages.output: Complete post with structured data, FAQ, charts
pipelineStages.guard: Template phrase scan + word count check

pipelineStages.name: Quality Gate
pipelineStages.onFail: Discard and regenerate (don't patch — patches accumulate AI artifacts)

pipelineStages.name: Publish
pipelineStages.output: Git commit + WebSub ping + indexing API submission
pipelineStages.guard: Repo lock acquired, rebase guard passed, [nobuild] tag applied

antiPatterns: Never let the writing model choose its own topic — that's how you get content cannibalization
Never let a content agent commit directly to git — always go through the pipeline with gates
Never retry a failed quality gate by tweaking the same output — regenerate fresh
Never run more than 3 agents concurrently — token waste from context switching outweighs parallelism gains
Never use Opus/Fable for mechanical tasks (formatting, link insertion) — that's Haiku's job
Never skip the cannibalization check to save time — a duplicate page is worse than no page
